prompt:
I need the front end for Leadloom. A research service for freelance journalists that searches recent coverage across thousands of publications and collects editors' open calls for pitches, so a writer can check whether a story has been done and find where to send it.

Who's using it: Priya Halvorsen, a self-employed science and environment writer for nine years who pitches 8–12 stories a month to magazines and newsletters and pays for the service herself from her freelance income.

What they're doing right now: A beekeeper source just told her about a new virus spreading through urban hives in three Midwestern cities. Before writing a pitch she needs to know whether anyone has covered it in the last six months and from which angle, which outlets have taken similar pollinator stories recently, and whether any editor has an open call that fits. Her first search returned 340 articles, mostly general bee-decline pieces. She wants to narrow to coverage of this specific virus or urban beekeeping, see what the service suggests from her saved interests, and leave with three outlets to pitch by Friday.

What's in the system at this point: An index of about 2.1 million articles from 4,800 publications, each with headline, outlet, author, date, section, word count, and whether the author was staff or freelance. 140 open editor calls, each with outlet, editor name, topics, pay rate ($0.50–$2.00/word or flat $300–$1,500), word count range, deadline (e.g. Dec 1) and posted date. Priya's profile: 7 saved searches (e.g. 'urban agriculture', 'invasive species Midwest'), 23 outlets she has written for with her history (last published, pay received, response time), 4 pitches currently out with their send dates. Relevant hits include a 600-word local TV story from September on hive losses in Milwaukee, a Modern Apiarist trade piece from October naming the virus, and two national pieces on pollinator decline from the summer.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
